sections.content:
You know *porque* from A1, *debido a* from B1 Unit 6, and *ya que* from A2 Unit 28. B1 Unit 32 added *como* at the start of a sentence. New here are *puesto que* ("since") and *dado que* ("given that"), and a clear picture of how the four differ.

• *porque* answers the question "why?" and gives the reason as new information. It usually comes after the main clause.
• *ya que*, *puesto que* and *dado que* give a reason that the listener already knows or accepts. *Puesto que* and *dado que* sound more formal.
• *como* gives the reason first, and then comes the result: *Como llovía, nos quedamos en casa.*

All of them state a real reason, so the verb is in the indicative.

sections.title: One reason, four ways
rows: Nos quedamos en casa porque llovía.
We stayed at home because it was raining.
Ya que estás en la cocina, prepara el café.
Since you are in the kitchen, make the coffee.
Puesto que nadie contestó, volví a llamar.
Since nobody answered, I called again.
Dado que el museo cierra a las cinco, tenemos que salir ya.
Given that the museum closes at five, we have to leave now.
Como llovía, nos quedamos en casa.
As it was raining, we stayed at home.

sections.content: A reply to *¿Por qué…?* begins with *porque*. *Como* and *ya que* put the reason before the result, so they do not work as a short reply on their own.
